description: Android usage-list window capabilities. Mobile registers four plugins, each granted only what the webview actually calls. Opener (issue #159): built-in sign-in hands the Claude authorize URL and Codex verification URL to the device's external default browser instead of loading them in the app's own WebView, so this grants only the "open URL" permission that flow needs — no tray, no autostart, no updater, no notifications (all later tickets per ADR 0006). Dialog (issue #152): credential export/import lets the user pick the export file in the system file dialog, so this grants the dialog's open/save entry points — and nothing from the fs plugin, whose commands stay uncallable from the webview: the export/import commands call its Rust API in-process with the URI the user just picked, so the webview can only ever touch a file the system dialog returned. Barcode scanner (issue #156): the desktop→phone QR transfer's scan/cancel/permission calls are driven straight from the webview's own JS API rather than an app-defined command, so this grants the plugin's whole `default` permission set (scan, cancel, check/request camera permission, vibrate, open app settings) — everything it exposes is already scoped to "read a QR code", with no filesystem or account access of its own. Every other command it calls (get_snapshots, set_config, qr_scan_frame, ...) is an app-defined command, not a plugin one, and app-defined commands aren't ACL-gated. `allow-open-url` only ENABLES the command; unlike desktop (which calls opener::open_url directly from Rust, bypassing the ACL) the mobile flow invokes it over IPC, so it is scope-checked. An empty scope forbids every URL, so we attach an allow-list restricted to the two OAuth hosts we actually open — the tight-scope equivalent of `opener:allow-default-urls`' blanket `https://*`.
